edits.find:
⚠︎ Primary HPV start age — the ledgers split Exam ledger (USPSTF, what the bank scores): primary HPV testing begins at age 30; 21–29 is cytology alone.
Clinic ledger (ACS 2020): primary HPV begins at age 25, every 5 years, preferred — which removes the 25–29 cytology block entirely.
Answer 30 on the exam. The age-21 floor is identical in both and is not in dispute — see Cervical Screening: the Age-21 Floor.

⚠︎ Primary HPV start age: exam versus clinical practice Exam answer: USPSTF (US Preventive Services Task Force) starts primary HPV (human papillomavirus) testing at age 30; 21–29 is cytology alone.
Clinical practice: ACS (American Cancer Society) 2020 starts primary HPV testing at age 25, every 5 years, as the preferred test. This removes cytology-alone screening at 25–29 entirely.
On the exam, primary HPV testing starts at age 30. The age-21 floor is the same in both; see Cervical Screening: the Age-21 Floor.

edits.find: The two traps in one stem Fibroids cause bleeding in premenopausal women; after menopause they involute. Atrophy is the most common cause of PMB (~60%) — but it is a diagnosis of exclusion, so "pale vagina with minimal rugation" does not license reassurance. And a progestin IUD is contraindicated in undiagnosed bleeding.
edits.with: Fibroids and atrophy after menopause Fibroids cause bleeding in premenopausal women; after menopause they involute. Atrophy is the most common cause of PMB (postmenopausal bleeding), at ~60%, but it is a diagnosis of exclusion. A "pale vagina with minimal rugation" therefore does not license reassurance. A progestin IUD is contraindicated in undiagnosed bleeding (IUD, intrauterine device).

edits.find: Stability picks the branch Hypotensive, rebound, or shoulder pain (diaphragmatic irritation from hemoperitoneum) → skip everything, emergent laparoscopy/laparotomy. Stable ectopic workup = image; unstable = operate — the same logic as PE.
edits.with: Stable versus unstable Hypotension, rebound, or shoulder pain (diaphragmatic irritation from hemoperitoneum) → emergent laparoscopy/laparotomy, with no further workup. A stable patient with a suspected ectopic gets imaging; an unstable patient goes to surgery. This is the same logic as in PE (pulmonary embolism).
